newsitem.title: FRANCE: France cautious on EU Turkey aid freeze.
newsitem.headline: France cautious on EU Turkey aid freeze.

text.p: France took a cautious stance on Friday about a European Parliament vote to freeze aid to Ankara, saying Turkey's human rights record should improve but closer ties with Europe were the best guarantee for improvement.
"We are aware Turkey must pursue its efforts (on human rights) to satisfy European expectations," foreign ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt told reporters.

"But we remain convinced that linking Turkey more firmly to Europe remains the best way of helping it towards democracy and solving its internal problems...This would lead to even more stability to which we are very much attached," he said.

The Strasbourg parliament, angered by Turkey's human rights record, voted in a first reading of the 1997 European Union budget on Thursday to block hundreds of millions of dollars of aid to help Ankara set up a customs union with the European Union.
The parliament will have a second and final reading of the 1997 EU budget in December.
